scorecard.name: Took ownership of the problem
scorecard.coaching: Although you manually credited the £180.00 trade-in value and closed the return flag, at [06:44] you disparaged S-Net's grading partner and told the customer to chase them herself: 'Honestly, our third-party grading contractor Assurant is a shambles—that's their mess not ours, and if you have any query about the physical handset inspection certificate you'll have to chase Assurant directly because I don't deal with their warehouse.'

grader.scenario: Trade-in credit of £180 for old iPhone 13 not applied to mobile upgrade bill 21 days after warehouse receipt
grader.notes: Single borderline FAIL on Ownership ([06:44]): Freya takes ownership of the £180 credit override, locks the return flag as Fulfilled, and confirms live that Cordelia's bill drops from £215 to £35 ([08:45]–[09:07]), but at [06:44] blames third-party contractor Assurant ('that's their mess not ours... you'll have to chase Assurant directly because I don't deal with their warehouse'). Per Section 7.2, doing other useful things in the call does not cancel an explicit deflection line.

items.name: Branding and Survey Check
items.evidence: [00:00] "thank you for calling S-Net Mobile Upgrades and Billing Support" and [10:46] "Thank you for choosing S-Net Mobile" plus survey check.

items.name: Hold time and Dead Air
items.evidence: No holds or dead-air gaps over 30 seconds occurred during the call.

items.name: Verified customer
items.evidence: [00:20] Freya verified the customer's billing address and four-digit security PIN before accessing the mobile account.

items.name: Personalized the call/ticket appropriately
items.evidence: [00:20] "Hi Cordelia, I would be glad to look into your iPhone 13 trade-in and get your mobile bill sorted out today."

items.name: Empathy & Acknowledgment Statement
items.evidence: [01:22] "I am so sorry for the frustration and shock of seeing a £215.00 bill when you sent your iPhone 13 back right on time three weeks ago, Cordelia—I completely understand why you want that £180 credit sorted before your Direct Debit goes out."

items.name: Paraphrasing
items.evidence: [01:37] "So just to make sure I have all the details straight: you returned your 128-gigabyte iPhone 13 via Royal Mail Tracked 24, it was signed for at the trade-in warehouse 21 days ago on 27 September, but the £180 trade-in credit was not applied to today's £215.00 bill."

items.name: Active listening
items.evidence: [02:53]–[07:27] Freya accurately recorded and used the Royal Mail tracking number (`JB482910385GB`), old iPhone 13 IMEI ending `8492`, and Direct Debit date (`24 October`).

items.name: Took ownership of the problem
items.evidence: [06:44] "Honestly, our third-party grading contractor Assurant is a shambles—that's their mess not ours, and if you have any query about the physical handset inspection certificate you'll have to chase Assurant directly because I don't deal with their warehouse."

items.name: Build rapport and observed professionalism
items.evidence: [01:22]–[11:04] Freya was warm, reassuring, and thorough with the customer across the call.

items.name: Probing
items.evidence: [02:03]–[02:26] Freya probed for the Royal Mail Tracked 24 tracking reference, the last four digits of the old iPhone 13 IMEI, whether Find My iPhone / Activation Lock had been disabled, and whether any grading query email had been received.

items.name: Confirmed the issue is resolved
items.evidence: [08:45]–[09:07] Cordelia refreshed the My S-Net app live on the call and confirmed her balance and 24 October Direct Debit dropped from £215.00 to £35.00, and confirmed receipt of PDF credit note `CN-7721904`.
